HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. KOREAN WEBTOON battle movie still. NIGHT GROUND. Wide iconic, figures true human size. ONE device: a dark ridge path as a hard diagonal. Goguryeo GAEMAMUSA mid-secret-march: horses fully skirted in red-and-black lamellar barding exactly as the mural ref, chamfrons, fringed red lower edge; riders in matching scale, conical helms with long BLACK plumes, long spears upright. Quiet dust, no torches on their side. Monumental. Copy the attached gaemamusa boards. No text. No watermark. BATTLE ACTION FRAME in the same painted look, NOT a calm posed still: a real battle caught mid-moment, like a frame from a big-budget animated war film. The camera is INSIDE the fight — low over the water among the oars, on a heaving deck, or at a hard dutch angle — with a dark out-of-focus foreground shape close to the lens (a gunwale, an oar blade, a shield rim, a banner, a burning spar). LOTS OF FIRE: sails and decks burning in painted flame with heat shimmer, columns of black and orange smoke, sparks and embers driving across the frame, firelight on wet faces and steel. ARMIES: dozens to hundreds of soldiers in frame at true human size against the ships — packed along gunwales, climbing, falling, rowing, loosing arrows — the nearest fully drawn and acting, the far ones massed painted shapes in the smoke. MOTION: spray thrown off oars and bows, arrows streaking in long lines, cloth, hair and banners whipping, bodies mid-leap and mid-fall, motion blur on the fastest things. EMOTION: every near face acts — screaming orders, terror, rage, grief, gritted teeth, soot and spray on the skin. WATER is a real painted sea — heavy dark swells, foam, fire reflected in it — never Hokusai claw waves, never woodblock or scroll stylisation, never flat cartoon shapes, never toy boats. The same ships, banners and shoreline in every frame of this battle. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: ref_gaemamusa (GAEMAMUSA: copy mural scale-barding, red-black skirts, chamfrons, long black plumes, upright spears; horse anatomy from damul_gaema board), obj_damul_gaema (GAEMAMUSA: copy mural scale-barding, red-black skirts, chamfrons, long black plumes, upright spears; horse anatomy from damul_gaema board), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
